scope: Review of the Firefox crash mitigation; test tooling and documentation only

findings.gap: Runner/lock/CI version agreement was not enforced
findings.resolution: Validate installed versions, root and nested lock copies, dependency edges, linked override and digest-pinned CI tag

findings.gap: Tag-filtered regression did not prove the triggering rule covered the affected elements
findings.resolution: Default axe rules, explicit labelled-region target assertions, named lookups before/after the scan and retained scan attachments

findings.gap: Contributor recovery and candidate-upgrade sequence was incomplete
findings.resolution: Document clean installation, matching-browser installation, sequential validators, focused reproducer and Linux upgrade acceptance

findings.gap: Changed Linux browser environment and existing pixel baselines lack execution evidence
findings.resolution: Retain the requirement; Docker unavailable and WSL not installed

validation.cleanInstall: npm ci --ignore-scripts passed; zero reported vulnerabilities

environment.limits: Checks version alignment and digest syntax; registry digest identity and Linux execution are separate checks.

priorEvidence.note: Historical execution evidence retained; the full suite and frozen app evaluation were not repeated in this review. Revised regression cases were rerun in all three engines.

limits: Version validation checks container digest syntax, not registry identity or Linux execution.
Default axe rules in the small regression fixture do not make other WCAG-tagged suites or consuming apps a full accessibility certification.
The upstream Firefox engine bug and property-only reference-label behavior are not fixed by this mitigation.
Linux pixel comparisons, hosted CI, native assistive technology and live design tools remain unverified in this review.
Designs, Midnight/dark default, runtime components, visual baselines and original trial apps are unchanged.
